title: Billable offsets audit and deterministic attribution for resumable fragment chains
creator: Riley Chen
description: Intermittent customer reports and audit traces show duplicated or missing billable token offsets when clients reconnect and resume long-running streaming requests. Symptoms: (1) final invoice ledger shows gaps where resumed fragments were not attributed, (2) duplicate credits when speculative fragments replay, (3) reconciliation job flags non-deterministic offsets across replayed sessions. Root cause hypothesis: the current session checkpointing uses a coarse session UUID + last-seen offset without a stable fragment identifier, allowing overlapping fragment replays and ambiguous attribution when the client and proxy perform partial retransmits or mid-session model substitution.
proposal: Introduce deterministic fragment-chain anchors: assign each emitted fragment a stable fragment_id (64-bit randomized + checksum of payload+parent-offset), persist fragment anchors in the session ledger at production time, and update per-session "confirmed_offset" only when a terminal ACK/finalization arrives. On resume, client-supplied resume_token is validated against fragment anchors; any re-transmitted fragments are deduped by fragment_id. For speculative fragments (server-side sampling), mark provisional token counts and only finalize to billable totals after confirm/finalization. Reconciliation job will use fragment anchors to deterministically map ledger entries to billing windows and to generate an idempotent retro-credit/charge plan.
tradeoffs: Pros: deterministic audit trail, idempotent replays, clearer reconciliation. Cons: additional metadata persisted per fragment increases ledger size and write amplification; slight increase in latency for first-fragment writes due to synchronous anchor persistence. Alternative (lighter) would be retain coarse-window checksums but that yields fuzzy attribution and complicates retro-credit logic. Chosen approach favors correctness for P0 customer-impacting billing anomalies; we will mitigate storage cost via compacted anchors and TTL of per-fragment metadata after reconciliation window (e.g., 7 days).
acceptance_criteria: Repro: Create regression test that reproduces duplicated/missing billable offsets from canned disconnect/resume sequences
End-to-end: For 1000 synthetic resumed sessions, final billed token totals must be identical after 0 and 5 simulated reconnects (determinism).
Reconciliation: Merge job can reconcile previously flagged invoices using fragment anchors and produce retro-credit plan with audit log entries per corrected invoice.
No regressions: Latency P99 for first-fragment write increases by <= 10ms in staging under baseline load.
Storage: Per-tenant ledger growth for anchors limited and reclaimed after TTL; monitor shows <5% storage increase on staging cluster during rollout.
test_plan: Unit: fragment_id generation and checksum validation (+ fuzz tests for collision resistance)
Integration: simulated client with mid-stream model switch, partial retransmit, out-of-order fragments; verify dedupe by fragment_id
E2E: deploy to staging with traffic shadowing from production for 48 hours and run reconciliation job differences comparison
Chaos: inject network drops at various offsets and assert invoices before/after reconciliation converge deterministically
Audit: long-running ledger export for sample tenant and manual verification of fragment anchors vs token tallies
rollout_plan: Feature gated: start with internal tenants -> limited beta (5 prod tenants) -> broad rollout. Steps: (1) deploy schema and anchor-writes behind feature flag, (2) run reconcile-mode where anchors are written but not used for billing, compare outputs for 72h, (3) enable anchor-backed billing in a small cohort, monitor discrepancies and latency dashboards, (4) full enablement and enable TTL compaction job after 7 days.
notes: We must coordinate with billing/legal before any retro-credit application for production tenants. Storage schema: use compact binary fragment_id and 16-byte checksum; store anchors in per-session append-only shard to simplify compaction. Need ops runbook for rollback (disable anchor-backed billing and revert to previous ledger snapshot).
